title: Peach and Ginger Shrub with Cider Vinegar and Soda
summary: Peaches simmer with sugar, water and ginger until soft, are mashed and strained, then the syrup is sharpened with cider vinegar and topped with soda water over ice.

ingredients.item: ripe peaches (or thawed frozen), stoned and chopped

steps.title: Cook the peaches
steps.text: Put the peaches, sugar, water and ginger in the saucepan and bring to the boil over high heat. Lower to medium-low, cover and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peaches are soft and falling apart.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and mash the peaches with the masher until evenly pulpy.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour through the sieve into the bowl, pressing hard on the solids to extract all the syrup, then discard the solids.

steps.title: Add vinegar
steps.text: Whisk in the cider vinegar, cool, then pour into the jar and refrigerate. You will have about 300 ml.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: For each glass, pour 50 ml shrub syrup over ice, top with 200 ml cold soda water, stir gently and add a peach slice if you like.

tips: The vinegar is added after cooking so it stays bright and sharp.
Ripe, fragrant peaches give the best flavour; frozen peaches work well out of season.
The shrub mellows over a few days in the fridge.
Adjust the ratio to taste: more syrup for sweeter, more soda for lighter.
storage: The syrup keeps in a closed jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
